name: Md. Ahasanul Adib
headline: Electrical Engineer · Power Systems, AI & Machine Learning
summary: I'm an electrical engineer from Bangladesh, working where power systems meet machine learning. I graduated from the Islamic University of Technology (IUT) in 2024 with a BSc in Electrical and Electronic Engineering. Since then I've worked as a Junior Engineer at the Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), where I turn GIS data from real distribution networks into ETAP models for load-flow and short-circuit studies. Since October 2026 I also teach undergraduate EEE courses at Anwer Khan Modern University. My research so far covers a thesis on plasmonic coupling and heat generation in silver nanoparticles, and an IEEE conference paper on deep learning for colorectal cancer diagnosis. I'm now applying for funded PhD positions (research or teaching assistantships) in power systems, AI and machine learning, renewable energy, photonics and plasmonics, and biomedical engineering.

projects.title: GIS-Based Distribution Network Modeling and Analysis Using ETAP
projects.subtitle: Turning GIS data from real 11 kV feeders into simulation-ready ETAP models at BPDB.
projects.description: Electrical distribution feeder models built in ETAP from real-world GIS data: topology, conductors, transformer ratings, line lengths and connected loads.
contribution: Extract and prepare **GIS data** in ArcGIS Pro for feeders, substations and consumers, ready for electrical system design.
Build **feeder and substation models in ETAP** from the GIS network: topology, conductor specifications, transformer ratings, line lengths and connected loads.
Prepare the models for **load-flow, voltage profile, feeder loading and short-circuit studies**.

projects.title: Plasmonic Coupling and Thermal Effects on Photothermal Response of Randomly Distributed Nanoparticles
projects.subtitle: Undergraduate thesis, Islamic University of Technology.
projects.description: Modeled how plasmonic coupling and thermal accumulation change heat generation in randomly distributed silver nanoparticles, using DDA and the thermal Green's function.
contribution: Used the **discrete dipole approximation (DDA)** to model electromagnetic interactions between randomly placed silver nanoparticles.
Calculated the spatial **temperature distribution** with the thermal Green's function.
Found that **plasmonic coupling** can strongly increase heating away from an isolated particle's resonance, while reducing the temperature rise at resonance.

projects.title: Parkinson's Disease Detection Using Machine Learning
projects.subtitle: Classifying Parkinson's disease from voice measurements.
projects.description: Compared SVM, Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosting and an MLP on 195 voice recordings. The MLP reached 89.74% mean accuracy and a 93.22% F1-score.

projects.title: Economic Load Dispatch Using MATLAB
projects.subtitle: Three methods for the cheapest generation schedule, compared.
projects.description: Implemented Lambda Iteration, Newton's method and Dynamic Programming in MATLAB, then compared speed and accuracy with generator limits and transmission losses.

projects.title: Pulse Width and Frequency Measurement Using an 8052 Microcontroller
projects.subtitle: Frequency and duty cycle measurement with signal generation.
projects.description: An 8052-based system that measures frequency and duty cycle, compares two inputs and outputs a signal at their sum. A 10 kHz input read as 10,010 Hz (about 0.1% error).

projects.title: Sudoku Solver Using Python
projects.subtitle: A graphical Sudoku solver using constraint satisfaction and backtracking.
projects.description: An interactive PyQt5 application where users enter a puzzle and see the solution, built on constraint satisfaction, graph-based candidate selection and backtracking.
contribution: Contributed to the **code implementation** of the solver and its interface.

projects.title: Automatic License Plate Recognition Using MATLAB
projects.subtitle: Reading plate characters from images with image processing and ANFIS.
projects.description: Image preprocessing, morphological operations, geometric feature extraction and ANFIS character recognition, tested on about 30 sample images.

projects.title: Regenerative Braking System Simulation in MATLAB
projects.subtitle: How an electric vehicle can recover braking energy.
projects.description: A design study of a DC shunt motor and buck converter system that recovers kinetic energy during braking and stores it.

experience.position: Junior Engineer, GIS Based Distribution Network System project
highlights: Extract GIS data across distribution zones using ArcGIS Pro and prepare feeder, substation and consumer datasets for electrical system design.
Build feeder and substation distribution network models in ETAP.
Run load-flow and short-circuit studies and write technical reports with recommendations.
Visit substations to check equipment and relay setting data against field conditions.
Work on relay coordination, voltage regulation and loss reduction, and present data-backed findings to stakeholders.

experience.position: Adjunct Faculty, Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
highlights: Electrical Circuits I / Basic Electrical Engineering (EEE 1201, theory): circuit laws and network theorems, transient and steady-state analysis, phasors and AC circuits, three-phase systems.
Basic Electrical Engineering Sessional (EEE 1202, laboratory): circuit measurements, verification of Thevenin's theorem and maximum power transfer, RLC resonance, three-phase power measurement.
Energy Conversion I (EEE 221, theory): transformers and three-phase and single-phase induction motors, equivalent circuits, tests, starting, braking and speed control.
My teaching focuses on mathematical problem-solving, theoretical foundations and practical engineering applications.
Taught Physics and Mathematics and mentored students in problem-solving.
